Messages.Author: Jack Crow
Messages.Body:
Meth A,B, Me

If I hunt, another Methuselah (A and/or B) may play a reaction cards
on their minions.

If I call a referendum, this should also be the case.

Is there any way that I can play a reaction card on a minion of mine
during one of my own actions? (that you can think of)

Messages.Author: Derek Ray
Messages.Body:
On Sun, 22 Jul 2001 14:24:34 GMT, no...@nowhere.com (Jack Crow) wrote:

>Is there any way that I can play a reaction card on a minion of mine
>during one of my own actions? (that you can think of)

No. One would think this would be obvious from a simple perusal of
section 1.6.3 of the rules, excerpted below:

"...5. Reaction cards: A ready untapped minion can play a reaction
card in response to an action TAKEN BY ANOTHER METHUSELAH'S MINION (an
action taken by one of a Methuselah's minions cannot be reacted to by
any of her own minions)..."

This was taken directly from a Final Nights printed rulebook.

-- Derek

I don't know about y'all, but it worries me a great deal that someone
who intends to code ANY sort of client for V:TES is -so- unfamiliar
with the game mechanics. The jury is still out for now, mostly
because I don't see anyone else doing anything at all, but ...

Messages.Author: Derek Ray
Messages.Body:
On Sun, 22 Jul 2001 18:48:31 GMT, no...@nowhere.com (Jack Crow) wrote:

>>Meth A,B, Me
>>
>>If I hunt, another Methuselah (A and/or B) may play a reaction cards
>>on their minions.
>

>Can more than one reaction card be played by methuselah B in response
>to an action?

Technically? No. Methuselahs do not play reaction cards.

Again from 1.6.3:

"...5. Reaction cards: A ready untapped minion can play a reaction

card in response to an action taken by another Methuselah's minion."

So it's a Methuselah's MINIONS who play the cards, an important
distinction. If B has two or more untapped minions, each can play as
many reaction cards as they like, subject to 1.6.3, where we find (a
bit further down):

"A minion cannot play the same reaction card more than once during a
single action."

...indicating that multiple reaction cards are, indeed, playable by
any given minion, as long as they're different.

-- Derek

Of course, if you played the game at ALL, you'd know this shit.

Messages.Author: Jason Bell
Messages.Body:
"Jack Crow" <no...@nowhere.com> wrote

>
> My problem is that the 1.6.3 states that a minion may play "a reaction
> card" in response to an action. So I need to know if it's 1 reaction
> card per action or 1 reaction per action or modifier. The implication
> of "cannot play the same reaction card" is technically, ambiguous. I
> cannot assume one way or the other, although I am aware of standard
> interpretation...I'm not interested in seeing another "Independent
> Votes" problem.

Yes, it is not difficult to read 1.6.3 as implying that a player can
only play a and only a reaction per action per minion, especially since
the description of action modifiers above it makes it more clear that
multiple action modifiers can be played during an action (in what
could be read as contrast).

This is made more difficult, as I could not find an example
or reference in the rule book where a reacting minion plays
multiple reaction cards.

In an only slightly alternate universe, the same text
could describe a rule where only one reaction is allowed
per minion, and the extra text in 1.6.3 would cover
circumstances where certain cards could give the ability
to play more (in this slightly alternate universe, Wake with
Evening's Freshness would be one of those cards that allows
another reaction card to be played, and the extra text in
1.6.3 would be a reminder that you could not play another
Wake even under Wake's ability). Unfortunately, in this
slightly alternate universe, you still would have been subject
to the same abuse by the same posters, just in service of the
exact opposite explanation.

But I believe the answer to your question is this:
Any number of the minions of any methuselah other than
the acting minion's methuselah may play any number of
reaction cards, excepting certain restrictions: one minion
cannot play the same reaction card by title more than once per
action, minions attempting to block cannot use a reaction
card to add intercept if they do not currently need intercept
(and I suppose cannot use intercept at all until an attempt to
block is declared and passes into the "currently failing due to
lack of intercept" basket), other restrictions particular to
other cards currently in effect, and perhaps one or two
conditions that have slipped my mind.

- Jason Bell

Secundus:

Rulebook text, taken from http://www.white-wolf.com/vtes/rulebook/:

"1.6.3.5

Reaction cards: A ready untapped minion can play a reaction card in
response to an action taken by another Methuselah's minion (an action

taken by one of a Methuselah's minions cannot be reacted to by any of her

own minions). A minion cannot play the same reaction card more than
once during a single action. A reaction card does not tap the minion using
it."

Let's examine that paragraph for any restrictions on the play of
reaction cards, by name or number.

The first sentence does not limit the play of reaction cards by name
or number. I hope we can agree on this one at least.

The second sentence restricts the reacting minion's ability to play
reaction cards by name. Specifically, it restricts a given reacting
minion to playing one of a named reaction card per action. It imposes
no additional restrictions.

The third sentence does not limit the play of reaction cards by name
or number. Again, that ought to be pretty clear.

No ambiguity. You may play any number of reaction cards on a given action,
as long as each untapped minion plays no more than one of each name.

Which was my paraphrase, if you'll be so good as to recall.

>Third, even your explanation is ambiguous as to total number
>of reaction cards allowed per action.

Tertius: No it isn't, as it's a paraphrasing of the rulebook's
non-ambiguous text.

gomi

It's not neccessarily distinct.

If my housemate asks me to get him "a" drink and I agree,
have I agreed to be his butler all night? Forever? I think not.
"A" is singular, and if you want it to mean iteratively singular,
the rules should state it explicitly, or at the very least,

take abuse for it.

to have a heck of a bleed deck abusing the "After playing this card,
you cannot play another action modifier to further increase the
bleed for this action" by playing all my bleed modifiers simultaneously.

>Or if it's not inconsistent, I'm going
>to have a heck of a bleed deck abusing the "After playing this card,
>you cannot play another action modifier to further increase the
>bleed for this action" by playing all my bleed modifiers simultaneously.

You cannot play two effects simultaneously in that manner in V:TES. A
card is played, it resolves[0] and then another opportunity exists to
play a card.

There is no concept of interrupt stack, or similar, as has existed in
Magic at various points.

[0] Actions and strikes being the obvious exceptions, with delayed
resolutions due to the manner in which they work.
